full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J.:- The instant Rule was issued calling upon the judgment-debtor opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned Order dated 18.02.2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Money Execution Case No. 01 of 2009 rejecting decree-holder's application under Order XXI, rule 54(1) read with Section 46 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for attachment of the judgment debtor's property and for issuance of precepts to this effect, shall not be set aside. 

 2. The material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, as has been stated in the revisional application, in short, are that the decree-holder-petitioner entered into 2 separate contracts dated 16.11.2000 and 14.02.2001 with the judgment-debtor-opposite party. In those contracts the parties incorporated the Rules of Arbitration as per bye-laws and rules of the Liverpool Cotton Association, agreeing to settle of their disputes arising out of the contracts through arbitration. Accordingly the disputes arose between the parties in respect of contracts and then it was referred to the Liverpool Cotton Association for Arbitration. The Arbitral Tribunal after hearing of the parties passed the award on 25.9.2002 in favour of the decree-holder. In pursuance of the award dated 25.9.2002 the Awardee on 30-8-2005 obtained an order from the Royal Courts of Justice, Admiralty and Commercial Registry, England to make the award Rule of the Court. Thereafter Awardee served a notice on 20.2.2006 through its local Counsel upon the judgment-debtor to comply and satisfy the aforesaid award. However, the judgment-debtor neither took any steps to set aside the award nor settled and satisfied with the said award. In the prevailing facts and circumstances the Awardee decree-holder for realisation of Award money filed Money Execution Case No.1 of 2009 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka, Bangladesh for execution of the award dated 25.9.2002. The learned District Judge registered the application as Money Execution Case No.1 of 2009 and started the execution proceeding by issuing summons upon the judgment-debtor. 

 3. While the said execution case was so pending, the Awardee decree-holder on 17.9.2009 by filing an application under Order 21, rule 54(1) read with Sections 46 and 151 of the Code Civil Procedure sought for attachment of the judgment-debtor's property located in the District Chuadanga and further prayed for an order for issuing precepts and send to the learned District Judge, Chuadanga for execution of the precept. The judgment-debtor appeared in the Money Execution Case and contested against the application for attachment and issuance of precepts by filing a written-objection. The learned District Judge after hearing both the parties rejected the application by his impugned order dated 18.2.2010. Hence, the decree-holder as petitioner was compelled to file the instant revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule with an order of injunction. 

 4. Mr. Ramzan Ali Sikder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the learned District Judge, Dhaka committed an error of law in rejecting the decree-holder's application for attachment of the judgment-debtor's property and issuance of precepts holding, inter alia, that admittedly the Court is a transferee Court and it is well settled that a transferee Court is not competent to issue precept. According to Mr. Sikder it was not only erroneous but misconstrued the definition, scope and enforceability of "Award" and "judgment" and "decree" as has been provided in the Arbitration Act-2001, and as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the Court below committed error of law as well as failed to appreciate that the Award of Liverpool Cotton Association was subsequently made Rule of the Court of the Royal Courts of Justice, Admiralty and Commercial Registry, England, which is according to the Arbitration Act, 2001 enforceable in Bangladesh by filing execution case before the learned District Judge, Dhaka assuming as the decree passed by, the District Judge, Dhaka and as such," the learned District Judge committed an error of law in rejecting the application for attachment of the judgment-debtor's property and issuance of the precepts. He further added that view taken by the learned District Judge that precepts only can be issued by the Courts, who passed the decree is not controversial but if the execution case arises out of a foreign Arbitration Award the learned District Judge ought to have considered and read the provisions of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 together with the Section 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submitted that the learned District Judge took erroneous view and committed an error of law in holding that the Court itself was a transferee Court as to the decree in question. Therefore, he rejected the application on a misreading of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He further added that the learned District Judge failed to construe the provisions of the Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 in its legal perspective for which he came to a wrong decision and consequently passed the impugned order rejecting the application for attachment and issuance of precepts which is clearly against the spirit of aims and objects of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001. Mr. Sikder lastly prayed to make the Rule absolute after setting aside the impugned order. 

 7. On perusal of the records and the annexures appended to the instant revisional application it reveals that the legal issue before the Court below was whether under Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 the award in question filed before him to be deemed a decree of the Court itself or the transferee Court. On perusal of the impugned order and the opinion formed by the learned District Judge, it appears that the Court itself decided that it is a Court of transferee. From the impugned order it further appears that the Court below opined that a transferee Court cannot issue a precept according to Section 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Therefore, the Court below comes to a conclusion that the application filed by the decree-holder is not competent to issue precepts. 

 "S. 46.(1) Upon the application of the decree-holder the Court which passed the decree may, whenever it thinks fit, issue a precept to any other Court which would be competent to execute such decree to attach any property belonging to the judgment-debtor and specified in the precept. 

 (2) The Court to which a precept is sent shall proceed to attach the property in the manner prescribed in regard to the attachment of property in execution of a decree. 

 Provided that no attachment under a precept shall continue for more than two months unless the period of attachment is extended by an order of the Court which passed the decree or unless before the determination of such attachment the decree has been transferred to the Court by which the attachment has been made and the decree-holder has applied for an order for the sale of such property." 

 (b) a foreign arbitral award shall, on the application being made to it by any party, be enforced by execution by the Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, in the same manner as if it were a decree of the Court. 

 On a bare reading of Section 45 of the - Arbitration Act, 2001 it appears that the foreign Arbitral award if any submits before the learned District Judge to execute the same as per provision of sub-section (b) of section 45 of the said Act, it will be tantamount to the decree of the Court before  which it is filed. 

 10. We are of the view that the learned District Judge, Dhaka, who started the execution proceeding to execute a foreign Award is not a Court of transferee, rather, within the purview of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 the learned District Judge, Dhaka itself ought to have assumed the Award in question is a decree of his own. However, refusing to accept the foreign Award as the decree of the Court below a clear misconception of law In view of the discussions and reasons made above, we are of the view that the Court below committed an error of law in not allowing the application filed by the decree-holder under Order 21, rule 54(1) read with Sections 46 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
